utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, good morning. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning to you. Mr. Oric, good morning. Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may please take a chair. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben senior trial attorney, together with co-counsel Gramsci Di Fazio, and our case manager, Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning to your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic together with Mr. John Jones. I represent Mr. Naser Oric. Together with us are our legal assistant Ms. Jasmina Cosic and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. And good morning to you and your team. So are there any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I've just signed before the sitting the decision on he adjudicated facts, so it should be available. We have all -- also discussed this morning the Prosecution response to the Defence response on the application of the Rule 92 bis (C) to the evidence or to the statement of Mr. Bogicevic. I think for practical reasons until we finish the process of having Mr. -- the other person - I'm not going to mention the name - examined by the doctor, medical doctor that you have agreed upon, since we don't know when that's going to happen and when we will have the report, and since I will be travelling, as I told you, the day after tomorrow, we've decided to split the decision into two. We will decide by tomorrow the motion as regards the dead witness. And we will reserve the position with regard to the other witness, pending the outcome of the medical certification. Okay. So that's it. If there is the need for decisions to be taken while the Trial Chamber is not sitting, I have made arrangements and that will be possible. In other words, even without my presence here in The Hague, I will be making use of an electronic signature so that anything that needs to be decided during the break will be decided. In other words, there will not be any time lost. So I think, Madam Usher, if you could be kind enough to bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I hope you have had enough time to rest after last Friday's testimony. Today we will certainly finish with your testimony. Madam Usher is going to give you again the text of the solemn declaration. I would like you to read it out again -- aloud again and that would remind you that you are testifying under a solemn undertaking with us that you would be testifying the truth, nothing but the truth. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I, Stanisa Stevanovic, witness, solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Friday you described a few incidents that occurred in the area where you lived in April and May 1992, including the barricades in Mocevici, the incident related to the death of Mr. Milanovic, and also what happened in Zeleni Jadar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also in response to my question about the barricades in Mocevici, you said that the Serbs at that time held Srebrenica and that the local Muslims were afraid that tanks would come from that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is correct, that they were in Srebrenica that is, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the second half of April and the first part of -- or rather, the first third of May 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Because on the 8th of May, Goran Zekic was killed and that's when the Serbs left Srebrenica, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the truth is that until the 8th of May the Serbs held Srebrenica. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica is a municipality in which you lived. Your village belongs to the municipality of Srebrenica. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time you were certainly interested in what was going on in your municipality, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, did you hear that at that time in Srebrenica 75 Muslims from Srebrenica were killed or went missing, including 10 women?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were familiar with the situation in the area because you moved about and you were in touch with people, including people from Fakovici. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In mid-May you were in that area, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bradjevina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Friday you indicated Zanjevo to us on the map, one of the neighbouring Muslim villages. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a village in the local commune of Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But that village is close to your village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, seven or eight kilometres, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, what happened to the Muslims in Zanjevo on the 15th, 16th, and 17th of May? Have you heard anything about that perhaps?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that they left their homes, too, that they were fleeing as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that 300 people fled to the neighbouring forests?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many -- I didn't know how many and I didn't know even now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard that people did flee to the neighbouring forests?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they fled but I heard that they had fled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that three old men and two women were killed in Zanjevo itself?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you perhaps heard that 345 of them were captured and closed, confined, in the elementary school in Fakovici, the one that you indicated to us last time, and that they suffered terribly there. You had to know that.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How come I would have to know about that, Mrs. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until then there were no killings that took place or not every day in that area, rather?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Stevanovic, you describe in detail all the incidents that occurred in relation to the Serbs in your entire area. How come you haven't heard anything that has to do with the death and persecution of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, I am only talking about the local commune of Ratkovici, what happened around my hamlet. As for Fakovici, Zanjevo, Orlica, Togevo [phoen], I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you talked about Zeleni Jadar as well, the incidents there.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that when I said that I went to get my wife's mother and I couldn't get her out, so I went back. So this was near the school, near Pozorici [phoen]. So that's how far I got and then I had to come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now use the map again, the one that we handed in on Friday. D46 is the number, I believe. Can you just turn the map 180 degrees, please. That's right. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the map and could you please indicate the Muslim villages to us: Tegare, Zapolje and Orlica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's better if we zoom in. The right-hand central part of the map because that would make it -- zoom in, not zoom out. That would make it easier for the witness to point -- at least he can see the villages better in any case, because it's only Zapolje that stands out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Witness, Zapolje, Orlica - that is to say, both Donja Orlica and Gornja Orlica - and Tegare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, Madam Vidovic, he showed us these last time with the exception of Tegare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, yes. Your Honour, in relation to that I have a question. This is where I broke off last time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, is it correct that these Muslim villages were attacked on the 16th of May from the direction of Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that people were expelled from these villages, that women were raped, and that they were persecuted throughout May and June in that area?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I now ask you to show the Trial Chamber the area of Grabovacka Rijeka and Sase.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicates the extremity of horizontal line 86 the village of Grabovacka Rijeka. And the other village?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sase is in that area. Isn't that right, Witness? Perhaps it's not on the map, but isn't it correct that Sase is in that area. But I think it actually is on the map.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could I ask you to encircle that name, Sase, please and put your initials against it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the area of Grabovacka Rijeka and Sase was held by the Serb army in May?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no military in Grabovacka Rijeka. As for Sase, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is in the immediate vicinity of your village, Grabovacka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grabovacka Rijeka, yes. Sase, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear or see or know for that matter that in Sase there was a camp where numerous Muslims from these villages that we discussed were brought in, Orlica, Zapolje, Tegare?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something else now, Witness. You knew the family, the Markovic family. You mentioned their house last time.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several Markovics. I don't know which one you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Ognjen Markovic, nicknamed Bato?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Witness, isn't it, that on the 8th of May, 1992 you were in Podkorjen together with him when Podkorjen was attacked as well as the entire village -- Muslim village of Poznanovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, Mrs. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that you know many Muslims in Poznanovici and Podkorjen and they know you, too?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a number but not many. I know more people from Mocevici because it's closer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ognjen Markovic got killed that day in Podkorjen. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ognjen Markovic went missing when he went to Brezani as far as I know, not when Poznanovici was attacked. The attack on Poznanovici was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please place Defence Exhibit D45 on the ELMO. This is a list of killed fighters. The list of killed fighters from military post code Bratunac 7042 from 1992 to 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, could you leaf through the document and please look at number 298. 298, have you found it? Number 298 it says Markovic, father's name Andrija, Ognjen, born on the 20th of December, 1950 in Fakovici. Killed on the 8th of June, 1992 in the village of Podkorjen. Have you seen this, Witness? Number 298. Have you seen that? Could you please move the document to the left, please.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've seen it. Can you give me an answer, Mr. Stevanovic. What was Ognjen Markovic doing in the Muslim village of Podkorjen on the 8th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct that he was in the village. He was killed in the forest on his way to Brezani, not in the village as far as I know. He went missing until the present day he hasn't been found. People don't even know whether he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber who was Ognjen Markovic.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ognjen Markovic was a man named Ognjen. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You wish to say that Ognjen Markovic was in fact not a local commander?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. Had he been a commander, he would have been in Fakovici. The TO commander in Fakovici was Slavko Jovanovic and not Jovanovic and not Ognjen Markovic, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what I'm asking in relation to events in connection with the Serbs you answered the questions in the following way: You said on Friday that you heard the Muslims had attacked Oparci in early June 1992. How come you had never heard that the nearby villages of Podkorjen, Poznanovici, and Dedici had also been attacked in early June 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's always difficult for anyone to tell you why they don't know something. I don't know how black holes function in the universe. I don't know these things. And it's very difficult for a witness to say why it is that he doesn't now. He said that he didn't hear about these attacks. How can he explain how it is that he hasn't heard about them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are perfectly right, Mr. Di Fazio, but let him answer the question because basically it's a style of questioning that we are -- we have to deal with rather than the way that the witness answers. This is very typical of the area and of the tradition, legal tradition, that Madam Vidovic comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I am tolerating it. On the other hand, the witness has already stated that with regard to the attack on Podri -- whatever the name is, the attack was in 1993 and not in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think if you let me continue going the same way I am, it will make things easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because the witness would understand exactly what is being asked for. He is being asked to give an explanation. Rather than give an explanation, rather than a chance an opportunity to correct himself. So this is how it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. And I certainly don't wish to be, appear to be or to be nit-picking and jumping up to my feet all the time. However, I thought at that moment that it was really quite -- had reached the point where the witness should be protected and I should object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think the witness will feel that he is being harassed in the least, because this is quite typical actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: As Your Honours pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in Fakovici, and that is your own local commune, there was strong TO forces and the Bircanska Brigade forces. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, I must say this again, not in my local commune, which was Ratkovici and not Fakovici. I must say this again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you refer to as guards in Ratkovici, were those part of the TO Fakovici detachment?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Friday you described something about the 21st of June, 1992 for us and you stated, as you had in your previous testimony of 2000 - you will certainly remember that - you said that TO units had arrived from Fakovici and that together with the relatives of those that were killed and wounded they evacuated those that were killed or wounded. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that they arrived in Ratkovici. Along Mleca, not Grabovacka Rijeka to Ratkovici. I don't know who came because I wasn't there, but I heard they had arrived there to pick up those people over there. How many, I don't know. Some probably they picked up and some they didn't. In Fakovici I have some close relatives and in Opravdici as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day there was a TO unit from Fakovici present there, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was a TO unit or whoever. A group of persons arrived. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Let us please now move on to the attack of the 27th of June, 1992, the attack on Bradjevina. Witness, you and others from your village, did you resist the attackers?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, how do you imagine 12 people who have already been caught out in broad daylight? We weren't even in the trenches and we didn't have enough weapons to put up resistance to very many people who were attacking us from all sides. What sort of resistance do you imagine we would have been able to put up in a situation like that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any firing from the houses in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who would have been in a position to fire from inside the houses? That's my question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the answer is no?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Stevanovic, you are becoming a little bit aggressive. Madam Vidovic is doing her duty here. She has every right to put all the questions that the Trial Chamber allows to you. And you have every right to answer those questions according to what you believe is the right answer. But you have no right to start arguing with Madam Vidovic or to become aggressive in her regard. I will not let you do that. So cool down a little bit because otherwise we will have to deal with you in a different manner. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, I will now draw your attention to a testimony that you provided in 1994. You gave a statement to the investigating magistrate Vaso Eric in Zvornik on the 20th of December, 1994. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If his answer is no, that means that we have to clarify something. I have, Madam Vidovic, is copy of what purports to be a copy of that statement, both in the original language, in the Serbian language, with ERN 00652396. Perhaps we can make that available, show it to the witness. And then he --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he will first confirm to us whether that is his statement or not. Mr. Stevanovic, look at the document, please, particularly at the bottom of each page of that document. There is a signature in Cyrillic. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So look at the top -- first line of that -- of the first page of that document and that is after -- just below the title which basically reads out "record of witness interview." And there is the date there of the 20th of December, 1994, and also the indication of the town of Zvornik as being the town of the investigating judge, the investigating judge, Vaso Eric. Do you remember giving a statement to Judge Vaso Eric on the 20th of December, 1994? And if you do remember, where did you give that statement, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my recollection, I gave a statement at home to a man named Slavisa who was an investigator, but I was never in Zvornik. I was in Milici where I gave one and in Bratunac at the Vuk Karadzic school, but that was in the year 2000, as far as I remember. As for this specific statement, it was actually given when I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically that explains it. Because we had that with the previous witness as well. Where you have at the top of the page the indication of the words Zvornik, that's not indicating the place where the statement was taken but the place where the investigating judge works, in which the place of the court to which the investigating judge is attached. So I think you can go ahead, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, you did give that statement after all, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Back at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You signed that statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is a whole series of details in that statement in relation to you, to your family, to how many of you there are, as well as some facts that you referred to last Friday.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please look at page 5 of that statement from 1994, the page is 01905660 of the English version, paragraph 3. Witness, can you please locate page 5 in your copy. You said at the time: "Although we were not many, we tried to put up resistance. Although we were few, we tried to do whatever we could. Since the Muslim forces outnumbered us by a long shot and they had already entered the hamlet, we were forced to pull out any way we could. We went down as far as Grabovacka Rijeka and we waited for the attack to subside and for the Muslims to withdraw." In the same paragraph of that statement from 1994 you continued: "After about two o'clock I decided to go back to the village, alongside with Milan Arsenovic; Jovanovic, Milosav; Dragan Jovanovic; and Sreten Stjepanovic, all of them from Vranesevici. They had arrived to help. Near the corner of Zivko Stevanovic's house we found a body, a body that belonged to my uncle's brother, Stojan Stevanovic. We found the body of my cousin, Stojan Stevanovic. I realised that his throat had been cut." Mr. Stevanovic, you said on Friday that you saw him killed with your own eyes and you described a number of details in connection with that. You even went on to name the persons who did that. That was a complete fabrication, wasn't it, on your part?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also described an attack that in actual fact you never saw. Why did you decide not to tell the truth about this particular event, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you wish to say that you personally witnessed the killing and death of Stojan Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will again draw the witness's attention to this specific part of the testimony under consideration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please now have a look at pages 0652401, paragraph 3, of the B/C/S version of the same statement. This is page 01905661 of the English. I quote: "In the meantime we had captured one Muslim soldier who had been stealing the potatoes and beans in Petar Prokic's in the village of Ruljevici. His name is Mehmed Tiro born in 1967 in the village of Orlica. During his interrogation, he admitted that he had taken part in the attack against my own hamlet Bradjevina. Therefore, I also spoke to him. He then confessed that he had -- that Fikret Secic had cut my brother Stojan's throat, father Izmet from the village of Mocevici and so on and so forth." Mr. Stevanovic, this is an entirely different story from the one you told to this court on Friday, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you something. I didn't give this statement. I don't know who gave this statement and what exactly was done. I know that Sinisa from Zvornik came to see me at my place and question me. How my signature ever got here -- and this is a typewritten copy. He never brought a typewriter with him when he came to question me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, do you wish to say that you didn't have any contacts with Mr. Mehmed Tiro. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in touch with Tiro.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is in fact true, Mr. Stevanovic, is that you questioned Mr. Mehmed Tiro, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't me that did the questioning. I was only present when he was being questioned by others.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in this statement given, say, about two years after the events or perhaps one year after the original question, and I will give you a specific date, you described a number of details stating that you were the one who interviewed him?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how it was. You keep talking about something but what actually gets written down, recorded, is sometimes not the same as what was originally said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at the last page of this statement from 1994, the very last page. Can you look at the last sentence, please, it reads: "The transcript was read back aloud and it faithfully reflects what I said. I do not wish to go back to it. I hereby confirm its authenticity with my signature. The transcript was read back aloud and it faithfully reflects what I said." Is it true that that's what it says?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true. Because whoever refuses -- he is it that refuses to actually read what was written and states that he confirms the transcript's authenticity. I would have needed to go back to the transcript to check if everything was authentic in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, were you not a police officer in 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No,.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you working for the military security service back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said here that you captured Mr. Tiro when he was stealing potatoes and beans. Is that true? Is it true that Mr. Tiro was captured in your presence? Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my presence but he was captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why would a person who would write this kind of record write something of this nature? How could this person know that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know how this person found out?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, the truth is that on this critical occasion, together with Serb soldiers, you fired at a group of people, including Tiro and that you wounded him seriously.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is also true that you interviewed a man who was seriously wounded?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the clinic in Fakovici with Tiro.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of August, 1992, when all of this was happening, Mr. Mehmed Tiro was not alone when he was captured. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was captured when he was alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time he was not alone when he was shot at. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you attacked a group of people. Isn't that correct? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among these people, Mr. Stevanovic, was Bitici, Sacir, Mr. Tiro's brother-in-law or son-in-law. Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was also wounded on that occasion. He lost a leg. You walked up to him and used a submachine-gun to fire at him, at his head. Isn't that true, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, that is the reason why you changed your story here in The Hague, and you completely forgot about Mr. Tiro and everything you said in 1994. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question, Madam Vidovic -- I am going to repeat it myself. Mr. Stevanovic, the question that was put to you is the following: "Mr. Tiro is not the only person that you interrogated in this way. Isn't that right?" And you answered: "That's not correct." So, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also interrogated other Muslims, including Mr. Saban Jakupovic. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was with him in Srebrenica -- rather, in Bratunac. I wanted to see him. I went to see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in your statement given to the Prosecutor in the year 2000 you said that you interrogated Saban Jakupovic and you described that in detail. You said that you personally interrogated him.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was there and that I asked him about a few things and that there was also this man called Sinisa from Zvornik and who was interrogating him and I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why would you be interrogating Muslim prisoners at all, Mr. Stevanovic? You were not authorised to do that kind of thing. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not authorised for that kind of thing. But since he's a neighbour I wanted to see him, chat to him, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, Mr. Stevanovic, that actually in this way you abused many Muslims. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's also true that you frequently visited the prison in Skelani where Muslims were abused. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is where Mr. Tiro, Mehmed, ended up. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He's living in the United States alive and healthy. He was treated at the hospital in Uzice and he left, Mrs. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true that he is now in the USA, but when I said "ended up," I mean he ended up there after your interrogation of the prisoner in Skelani. Are you trying to say that that is not true?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Fakovici they took him to Skelani. There was this Territorial Defence in Fakovici, not in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question with the language. In English it appears "interrogation". Do you mean interrogation in a formal sense? Because the witness always answered that he asked. So I think there's a difference between asking and interrogating. So is it clear in the Bosnian language this difference between interrogation and asking or interviewing?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our language the word is "ispitivanje." It can refer to both. Investigation is one thing, but "ispitivanje" can mean interrogation within proceedings that take place in the police. Investigation is something that is judicial, that is part of the judicial system in our language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: When you asked him, you are asking him whether he interrogated these people, not only had a talk with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Correct, Your Honour. That's correct, yes. Precisely. That is what I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser. Thank you, Madam Vidovic, for the explanation. Let's proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, it is also true that you organised the guards in that area, in the area of Ratkovici. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you described in your statement of 1984 [as interpreted] what happened then, you said that the people from Vranesevici came to help on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Vranesevici is a nearby village that includes a nearby hamlet called Ruljevic.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Vranesevici had an entire Territorial Defence unit, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask the usher to put document number 00656808 on the ELMO. This is a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, Judge Eser is drawing my attention that on line 9 of the transcript which page, page 23, reads your statement of 1984. It should be your statement of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at this document. This is the Grabovacka Rijeka-Vranesevici Territorial Defence list from the document seized at the Bratunac Brigade. Please look at number 7, Milan Arsenovic, and number 21 Jovanovic, Dragan. Have you seen it, Arsenovic, Milan? And number 20 is Jovanovic, Slavoljub. And underneath that there is a sign that we customarily use when things are repeated. So the surname Jovanovic is repeated. And then it says Dragan. Now, my question is the following: These are men who you actually mentioned in your statement from 1994 as people who came with you from Grabovacka Rijeka to Bradjevina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mr. Stevanovic, together with you on that day the unit of the TO Vranesevici fought with you on that day against the Muslims. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be given a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's the next number, D47?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, D48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document is being admitted in evidence as Defence document or Defence exhibit D48. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, you mentioned that you had the impression that Vekaz Husic was the commander in everything that was going on. Where is he from?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. On Friday you said that after the attack on Bradjevina you stayed in Fakovici only for about 20 days and you then went to Serbia and you returned from there on the 6th of October, 1992. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the truth?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th I just crossed over to collect the dead from Fakovici and we returned to Serbia on the same day. And then on the 3rd of January, 1993, or the 4th, I was arrested and taken to Bratunac and recruited for the brigade. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I did understand you properly, that you said that you returned to Fakovici on the 6th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, that's not correct. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were present as a fighter in Fakovici and you were present in September, October, and November 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please place on the ELMO document number 01320796. The list of fighters from Fakovici for their personal incomes, September, October, November. Dated the 25th of January, 1993. It comes from the seized financial documents of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. Number 11 is Stanisa Stevanovic. That's you, right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were there in September and October and what you said on Friday is not correct. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, this is 1993, it's not 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mrs. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the title: "List of fighters from Fakovici for personal incomes." The date is the 25th of January, 1993. But, but, it pertains to September, October, and November. Isn't it correct that retroactively in January 1993 you received your personal income for the previous months of September, October, and November?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. After the fall of Fakovici, nobody stayed behind in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document is being tendered and accepted in evidence as Defence Exhibit D49.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to draw your attention again to the statement made in 1994, page 7 of our Bosnian Serbian version. Could you please take a look at it. You have the statement?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- or is it this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 1994 statement, yes. Page 7, paragraph 2. This is page 01905661, the last paragraph of the English version. You said then: "In the period up to the 5th of October, 1992, I was in the area of Fakovici where I happened to be when the Muslims attacked Serb settlements in this area from the village of Tegare to Kutjesi." So, Mr. Stevanovic, in your first statement that you gave in relation to these events you said precisely what the document I showed you a few minutes ago says, too. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you said on Friday about these events was a total fabrication then, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is true then, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that after the fall of Bradjevina on the 27th we went down to Fakovici because you couldn't cross the river. The boats had been pulled ashore.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stevanovic. I already know that. But why would you tell an investigating magistrate or anyone else for that matter at a time when you remembered these events much more clearly than two or three years ago, why would you have told them that you were in fact in the area? Why would they have written something like that unless you had actually said it?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea what they wrote. I couldn't say something that wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stevanovic. I'll move on and ask you something else. You were a soldier of the Bratunac Brigade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 11 of the B/C/S version of your July 2000 statement, if necessary I will show it to you, paragraph 4, which is page 10 of the English version. The statement paragraph 3. You said as follows: "On the 3rd of January, 1993, I was recruited for the Bratunac Brigade of the Republika Srpska army. The Bratunac Brigade had only four companies." Is that true, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many exactly it had and I did so. But on the 3rd of January, 1993, Momir Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just please answer my question specifically. Is it or is it not true that the Bratunac Brigade only had as many as four companies?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many it had. I don't know exactly, whether it was four companies. I know that I was sent to the 4th Battalion near Kravica as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stevanovic. We'll see about that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to have placed on the ELMO a document called: "The founding of the Bratunac Brigade." This document was also seized in the archives by the OTP. Can we please show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, for today and for the future unless the question of the origin of the document arises, in which case we will discuss it in the absence of the witness, I would like you to refrain from mentioning where you obtained this document or where whoever gave you this document obtained it from. Because that sometimes could influence the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Your Honour. I will abide by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the following page. The page number is 06586483. This is an excerpt from a document. I will quote a portion of it to you now. If you could please have a look, the portion that says -- have you looked at the document? Can you please have a look at the next page of the B/C/S, paragraph 2, which states: "The Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade was established on the 14th of November, 1992, pursuant to orders from the command of the 2nd Corps, strictly confidential number 2-67, dated the 13th of November, 1993 -- 1992," my apologies. 1992. I made the mistake myself. The document says 1992. Now, if you could please look at the numerical strength of the brigade, I think that's paragraph 3. It states that the numerical strength of the Brigade on the day is 2.288 military conscripts. And then we see the units enumerated, brigade, command, reconnaissance platoon, the military police platoon, the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalions, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th Battalions, a company of young soldiers, a logistics company, a 120-millimetre mortars company, a tank platoon with three tanks, a platoon of APCs, and a mixed artillery battery. Mr. Stevanovic, you were a soldier in this brigade. Are you aware of the fact that the Bratunac Brigade had these units?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not correct, Mr. Stevanovic, that these battalions were in fact part of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that there was a battalion that was billeted in Bratunac and that its zone of responsibility was between Kaolin and Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Do you want me to answer this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to move on to a different question for you then. You said that you were a member of the 4th Battalion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was that battalion stationed?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was near Kaolin further down towards the farm. I'm not sure what the name of that place was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the 4th Battalion we're talking about, Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only there very briefly. I'm not sure if it was the 4th, but I think so. I was there only briefly. Then I was returned to Radijevici and then I crossed over into Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However brief your stay there, you had to be aware of the exact zone of responsibility that it covered, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly where you stationed? What was your area of activity?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on a field when they brought me to the trench. I'm not sure what it was. We came to the school building to rest one night and then we returned again. That was Christmas time when Kravica fell. They picked us up. I don't know anything. It was in Serbia. They picked up whatever they could, and They brought these people to the front line. And that's the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document is being tendered and accepted as Defence Exhibit D50.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, in your statement dated July 2000 you said that your unit was part of the offensive launched by the Republika Srpska army, the one that occurred in March and April 1993. And you referred to it as the combined Serb forces. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the only way I could put it. But it's as I said earlier, they transferred me to Fakovici and there was a guard there and they launched the offensive. That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore -- therefore, there was an offensive that was in the offing, in a manner of speaking, by the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, back in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm wondering if my client is receiving interpretation because I'm not receiving any interpretation into the Bosnian language, although I have the right channel. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a responsibility of checking this. Mr. Stevanovic -- I want to make sure that everyone has been receiving interpretation. You have been able to follow what Madam Vidovic has been saying because it's on your own language. So it's a question of whether you were hearing her voice or not, which I take it you have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has anyone had any problems? I haven't and I take it that Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser haven't either because otherwise they would have certainly drawn up my attention. So the accused --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's fine now, Your Honour. It's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you said that there had been an offensive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please, I would like to have the following document placed on the ELMO. The number is 01321887 - 013218891. This is a combat order for further operations issued by the command of the Bratunac Brigade dated the 9th of April, 1993. This document was signed by the commander Colonel Cvjetin Vuksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please first of all look at the first page of the document. At number 2 it says, and I quote, have you found that? "The Bratunac Brigade, together with the Panther's Brigade and the special MUP unit, in cooperation with the Special Bircanska Light Brigade, enjoying strong artillery support, is attacking along the general axis: Zuti Most, Potocari, Srebrenica. The aim is to crush the enemy in the following areas: Bljeveca, Pale, Pecista, Likari, Srebrenica, and liberate the area along the axis of attack. Down the auxiliary axis: Ratkovici, Mocevici, Dimnici, supported by the BrAg of the Panthers." And can you also look at page 2 of the document. If you could look at number 4: "I decided that the main brigade forces, the Panthers Brigade, and the special unit of the MUP in joint action with the 2nd Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade would attack with a strong artillery support, the main direction Zuti Most, Potocari, Srebrenica, and use a part of the forces to attack along the auxiliary axis: Lemesac, Cizmici, Pale, Potocari, Sase, Azlica, Kvarac, Ratkovici, Mocevici, Stozersko, Pribicevac, in order to crush and destroy the enemy and liberate the areas along the above-mentioned axis." My question to you, Witness, is: Are these the combined forces that you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know about the unit that I was part of, the unit that came to Radijevici, and I was there guy as far as Mocevici and Brdo. And that's all I know about. Later I returned to organise the spring harvest, but I know nothing further about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which unit was that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, they call it the guard from Pjenovac. I'm not sure what the code name was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, in relation to this document can you answer the following question: Is it true that the forces that were operating in this offensive also included a strong artillery support in the re-taking of the entire Ratkovici area. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The forces that were part of the offensive that you confirmed, did those forces include a strong artillery support?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some artillery support from the village of Vranesevici, using two mortars as far as I know. We had returned from Mocevici, a group of us, about 15 persons from Fakovici, and then we were picked up again. I was left behind and the group was sent back to Kvarac. I'm not sure about the date. That was above Pribicevac

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore there was artillery in Vranesevici, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two mortars. That's the extent of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true then that this was what might have caused destruction to the buildings that were in the way of those artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How am I to say that? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be assigned a document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document is being tendered and accepted in evidence as Defence Exhibit D51. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have perhaps about 10 minutes left of my cross-examination, but I will request to go into private session after this. Therefore, I think this might be a convenient time for a break if the Chamber agrees obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Madam Vidovic. We'll have the break now. In any case we only had five minutes to go. We'll have the break now. We will reconvene at five minutes to 11.00 please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please briefly go into private session now? I have some photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D45 is a list, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the list and find number 557. The list is of soldiers who were killed, soldiers of the Bratunac Brigade, between 1992 -- rather, military post Bratunac between 1992 and 1996. If you could please look at the number 557. Have you found that? 557, Stojan Stevanovic, father Dragomir, born on the 28th of April, 1939, in the village of Ratkovici. On the 27th of June, 1992, he was killed in the village of Ratkovici. Therefore, this is a list of soldiers who were killed. Is it still your submission, Mr. Stevanovic, that this was a civilian person?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: At the time he could have been listed in any number of ways. All the victims claimed that they were soldiers in order to receive compensation. In terms of his age he could have been a soldier, but he was simply an alcoholic. That's what he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, did I hear you correctly? You said that all victims of war are now listed as ex-soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All male persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All male persons, but that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I know all of them and they're all receiving some sort of compensation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you expect someone who was killed to receive compensation?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But their families continue to receive compensation. All their families, all the families of victims who were killed are still receiving financial compensation for their deaths.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, but based on what are you saying this?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew this man, I talked to him, and he told me that he was receiving compensation. His wife is receiving compensation on his behalf, for example.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, on Friday you looked at and identified a number of buildings and features in various photographs. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In none of those cases did you actually witness how destruction occurred to any of those buildings, did you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't witness it for myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many damaged buildings did you actually see in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never counted them. I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What would your assessment be?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I know? I don't know how many houses there were. Even if I counted them one by one, perhaps I couldn't reach a definite figure, although I had lived in Fakovici for those eight or ten years.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many buildings were there in Fakovici? Could you give us a total, an assessment?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. Could we please place an exhibit on the ELMO. It is a list of households, flats, and farms across the municipalities and settled areas according to the 1991 census. This is also in relation to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the data as given in relation to Fakovici. Is it not true. Or do you know if it's true that Fakovici had 153 inhabitants, 54 households, 57 flats, and 33 farms? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. You said you knew Fakovici well. You did confirm that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, you must know that until the beginning of war there were 33 Muslims living in Fakovici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Fakovici, but there are the villages of Abdulici and Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Fakovici. Is it your submission that there were no Muslims living there and that they did not own houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. Even as we speak there were no Muslims houses there. There are some in Abdulici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there are none as we speak which is natural. But, please, just answer yes or no. Is it your submission that back then there were no Muslims living in Fakovici? Abdulici is a different thing.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am saying there were none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Are you saying that you don't know that their houses were torched in April and May 1992, in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could they have been torched if there were none to begin with?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you claim they never were there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this statistics report as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And this document is being tendered and admitted in evidence marked as Defence Exhibit D52.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, on the 11th of July, 1995, you were in Potocari when, or rather where the greatest massacre of the Srebrenica tragedy took place. You separated the men from their families, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What are you trying to say, that you were not there?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You weren't there at all?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at Pribicevac but I was not at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The families of Huremovic and Zenunovic, do they mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they do. Not Zenunovic, Huremovic. I don't know about Zenunovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that you did not have any contact on that day with that family?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does this "yes" mean?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did not have any contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is the relevance? Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is very relevant. It has to do with the credibility of this witness. And during the proceedings you will see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, the witness claims that he was not there and you will see why. Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Is there re-examination, Mr. Di Fazio?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, if Your Honours please. Can the witness be shown the list of killed fighters, D45.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, I think I can make my point relatively quickly. If you look at the list, for example, in number 12 you will see that the man there described Vojislav -- sorry, my apologies. Under 13, Drago -- Milovan Dokic was born in 1935. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Go to 115, Bogoljub Eric. Number 115, Bogoljub Eric. Do you see that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. 115, 1-1-5. Mr. Bogoljub Eric. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It says that he --

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It says that he was born in 1914. Did you ever see any fighters in 1992 or 1993 in the Army of the VRS at about that age, whatever that was in 1914 -- 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think my learned friend is trying to make an argument through the witness. The witness doesn't know these people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he's asking a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We've also heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please don't interrupt when the witness is about to give an answer to an important question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So did you ever see any fighters who appeared to you to be the sort of men who might have been born a second decade of last century, 1914. Did you ever see any men of that age? Now, remember, 1992 is the period of time I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see any men fighting on behalf of Serb forces of any description whatsoever in 1992 or in 1993 who appeared to you to have been born in the 1920s, men of that sort of age?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who were either over 60 or approaching 60, in other words -- or 70. Sorry. Over 60 and approaching 70 or even over 70.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you know, Your Honour, all the people who were forced to go into the war had to fight. And those who were over 60, or rather just below the age of 60 -- or rather, those who were up to the age of 60 had what was called work obligation. And they didn't have to go to the front line. But those who were over 60 had to go to the front -- did not have to go anywhere. However, those up to the age of 55 had to go to the front line. Regardless of whether they were sick or not, they made them go there. Because the front line was always manned by old men, up to 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you see Stojan -- your cousin, the man who was killed in Bradjevina, at any time in 1992 and 1993, fighting on behalf of Serb forces of any description whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked questioned in cross-examination regarding a statement that you had given in 1994. Can you tell the Trial Chamber -- or you already have told the Trial Chamber that the statement was taken at your place, at your home. Can you remember who came to your home and how the statement was recorded?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, some man called Sinisa came and asked me to sign a piece of paper. And he said that he'd type it out later. I made a statement in pencil and he made inscriptions. So I was never asked to come to Zvornik or Bratunac to sign the typewritten paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How -- on how many occasions did you speak to him and give him information?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times. He came to see me several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Always about the statement?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only my statement. He asked whether there was anybody else who had been up there who could have made this kind of statement sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So on the several occasions that he came back and spoke to you, is it the case that he spoke to you about the content, what you'd said, of your statement and/or other people who might also help him by giving a statement?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the statement taken for, what purpose, what proceedings? Do you know? And if you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever sign it in company with a judge or a clerk?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry, would Your Honours just bear with me on a quick matter. Thank you. Can the witness now be shown the document listing the fighters from Fakovici. I'm sorry, if Your Honours please, I don't have the -- I'm not precisely sure which exhibit number it is. It will be either --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: D49, thank you. May I just look at it before it's handed to the witness. I just want to check it out and make sure we're talking about the same document. Yes, thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've told us about in your testimony of when it was that you actually held a position in the -- in the armed forces -- the Serb armed forces and you said it was from January of 1993 onwards. While you were actually holding that position did you receive any salary, that is from January 1993 onwards, any salary or any money, any recompense for your activities as a soldier? Did they pay you from time to time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Prior to that, prior to January of 1993, had you ever received any salary or recompense from institutions of the VRS, pay salary, pay office or somehow get any payment of salary from the VRS before January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Look at the names that -- of the people in that document. Do you know any of those people, apart from number 11 which is your name? Do you know them? Go through them one by one.

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Milanovic, Slobodan, from the village of Tegare. Ilic, Milan, from Tegare, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know if there are any other men mentioned in that document, including ones where there's been a line been drawn through them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the working platoon from Fakovici, the one that I was on in 1993. When I returned from Mocevici, we were supposed to organise the spring planting and sowing. So this is work obligation. All of them were old men basically, and I was supposed to organise this agricultural activity in the spring, but Fakovici otherwise had more people than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. How old were they? Can you be a bit more exact, a bit more precise? Let's start with number 1, Mr. Slobodan Milanovic. Have you got any idea about how old he might have been in 1992?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 50-something, say 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about the others? Are there any men there that you know --

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilic, Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. About how old was he?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilic, Milan, is an elderly man. He may even be close to 70 now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So he was not yet 60 in 1992, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Continue down the list. Are there any men there that you see, are there any men there that you see in that list who in 1992, back then, back in the war, were clearly men in their 60s or 70s?

utterances.speaker: STANISA STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilic, Pero, he was a youngish man as far as I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. I'm not asking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
